name: Employment Hero
summary: Modular HR, payroll and recruitment platform for small and mid-size employers.
best_for: Australian and New Zealand employers who want HR and payroll from one vendor and will use both, where the per-employee rate beats separate systems
skip_if: you are budgeting in US dollars (the page is Australian, in AUD excluding GST, with no US equivalent) or you only need one of the modules, since each is sold separately and priced as though you are buying the platform
honest_knock: There is no such thing as the Employment Hero price, and the first thing to fix is the currency: the pricing page is the Australian one, its disclaimer reads 'All prices AUD ex. GST', and there is no US page. Then the structure. HR, recruitment, chat and payroll are separate subscriptions, most of them per employee, with a stated minimum of ten users underneath, so a six-person company is billed for ten. Payroll is back as its own plan at A$10 (read 20 November 2026), with SMS, superannuation and Heroclear fees on top, and Managed Payroll is an A$21-a-head add-on with a A$420 floor. And the recruitment tiers meter AI video interviews rather than people, with credits that reset monthly, do not roll over, and overage billed automatically with no hard cap.

pricing.entry_price_terms: HR Essentials · per employee per month excluding GST on the Australian pricing page, which is the default one and has no US equivalent
pricing.notes: (read 20 November 2026 on employmenthero.com/pricing/, the Australian page (hreflang en-au); first read 28 August 2026, re-verified 6 October 2026) The page's disclaimer reads 'All prices AUD ex. GST'. Separate pages exist for the UK, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia and Canada, and there is no US one. Sold as separate modules rather than one plan. Recruitment: Pro 50, Pro 100 and Pro 200 at A$199, A$359 and A$639 a month for 50, 100 and 200 AI video interviews, unchanged since August. The free ATS tier at A$0 with 50 one-off complimentary interviews that the page showed in August was no longer on it on 6 October 2026, in the served HTML or in a browser render. The disclaimer also names a 300-interview plan but publishes no price for it. Those are annual-billing rates: the disclaimer gives A$2,388 a year for the 50-interview plan at a 20% discount, against A$249 a month on monthly billing. Interview credits reset monthly, unused credits do not roll over, and overage is billed automatically with no hard cap. No HR or payroll subscription is required for Recruitment. HR Essentials A$11 and HR Engage A$15 per employee per month, each A$1 more than on 6 October 2026 (A$10 and A$14); the cards print the bare amount with 'Conditions apply'. HR Elite and Employment Unlimited are quote-only. A standalone Payroll plan is back on the page at A$10 (unlimited pay runs, automated tax calculations, award interpretation, payroll reporting, employee self-service); the card prints no unit, and SMS charges of A$0.18 per SMS, superannuation payments of A$0.30 per employee per batch and Heroclear at A$0.20 per employee per batch come on top. On 28 August and 6 October 2026 there was no standalone payroll plan on the page. Managed Payroll is an add-on at A$21 per employee per month with a A$420 monthly minimum (A$20 and A$400 on 6 October). Other add-ons, each per employee per month with a stated monthly minimum, all raised since 6 October: Chat A$2.50 (min A$25), Rostering and Time and Attendance A$5 (A$50), HR Advisory A$15 (A$300), Learning 10-course bundle A$9 (A$90), LMS Plus A$18 (A$180), EAP Standard A$9 (A$90), EAP Premium A$11 (A$110). Add-on contract costs are based on the greater of the minimum contractual amount and the actual billable employees each month. A minimum of 10 Users applies to every plan, billed on the higher of the users named in your agreement or the billable users. Every price on the page carries an asterisk.
